newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo stocks end flat, volume up on foreign buy.
newsitem.headline: Colombo stocks end flat, volume up on foreign buy.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed flat as buyers were hit by poor demand, but turnover was supported by foreign buying, brokers said.

The all share index closed 0.13 points up at 727.45. Hayleys Exports rose two rupees to 60, CTC Eagle Insurance one to 54. Turnover was 56.2 million rupees, led by foreign buying of 517,400 shares of Tokyo Cement.

"The investor was probably making a long-term investment. A cement stock is bound to do well if the economy grows at an average of six percent, as forecast, in the next few years," said a broker who declined to be identified.
The rest of the markt was dull as buyers were unable to get stocks due to a lack of sellers, brokers said.
"I had an order to buy over 50,000 shares of a pricey blue chip, but was unable to conclude the trade because sellers were holding out about 10 rupees above the current market price," said one.
Since first quarter 1997 corporate results which have come out so far have been healthy, sellers are demanding premiums for stocks, brokers said.
